rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Apparent expansion equals absolute expansion. ✅ Apparent expansion is LESS than absolute expansion because the container also expands. $\gamma_{app} = \gamma_{liq} - \gamma_{container} < \gamma_{liq}$.  ·  ❌ The apparent expansion of a liquid is independent of the container material. ✅ The apparent expansion DEPENDS on the container. A liquid in a copper container ($\gamma_{Cu} \approx 51 \times 10^{-6}$) shows less apparent expansion than in glass ($\gamma_{glass} \approx 27 \times 10^{-6}$).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Water expands uniformly when cooled from 10°C to 0°C. ✅ Water CONTRACTS when cooled from 10°C to 4°C (reaches maximum density at 4°C), then EXPANDS from 4°C to 0°C. This anomalous behavior is unique among common liquids.  ·  ❌ A liquid's absolute expansion can be measured directly with any container. ✅ It CANNOT — the container always expands. You must either use a container with negligible expansion (impossible) or apply the correction $\gamma_{liq} = \gamma_{app} + \gamma_{container}$.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The anomalous expansion of water was first studied by Daniel Bernoulli in the 18th century. It remains one of the most important anomalies in nature, making life on Earth possible.  ·  The weight thermometer method for measuring liquid expansion was devised by Dulong and Petit in 1816. It remains the standard laboratory method for determining coefficients of cubical expansion.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Why liquids need special treatment:** Unlike solids, liquids cannot maintain a fixed shape and must be contained. When heated, BOTH the liquid and the container expand, making direct measurement of liquid expansion impossible without correction.  ·  **Absolute (real) expansion:** The actual increase in volume of the liquid itself, independent of the container. $\Delta V_{abs} = V_0 \gamma_{liq} \Delta T$, where $\gamma_{liq}$ is the coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid.  ·  **Apparent expansion:** The observed increase in volume of the liquid as read from the container's scale. Since the container also expands, the scale marks move apart, making the liquid level appear to rise LESS than it actually does.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Key Formula 5: Important relation in Liquid expansion: absolute and apparent  ·  ❌ The weight of the liquid changes when heated. ✅ The MASS is constant. Only the volume changes. The weight thermometer measures the mass of liquid expelled, not its weight changing.  ·  ❌ All liquids expand when heated. ✅ Most liquids expand, but water between 0°C and 4°C CONTRACTS. Some alloys (like invar) also show anomalous expansion behavior over certain temperature ranges.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Ice floating is due to water's density being the same as liquid water. ✅ Ice is LESS dense than liquid water (about 9% less) because water EXPANDS upon freezing. This is a direct consequence of the anomalous expansion below 4°C.  ·  Carefully distinguish between similar-looking concepts in liquid expansion.  ·  Pay attention to the conditions under which formulas and theorems apply.
